title: Ang 876–879: Ramkali begins
hook: Guru Nanak opens the calm raga
tomorrow: two more Gurus sing Ramkali. what does each one add?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the elephant: sent to crush, it bowed instead. Today the walk enters a new stretch, and a calm raga, Ramkali.

A friend's study setup: a ten-hour playlist, three apps, a color-coded planner, and somehow no studying yet. None of it is wrong. It just piles up, until the simpler question gets lost: what do you actually know? On ang 876, Guru Nanak opens raga Ramkali by listing everyone's methods, and then saying what he knows instead.
screen: `THREE APPS AND A PLANNER.` → `METHODS PILE UP.` → `WHAT DOES HE KNOW INSTEAD?`

segments.voice: In paraphrase: some read Sanskrit, some read the Puranas; some chant the Name on prayer beads, absorbed in meditation. Then: now or ever, I know nothing; I recognize only your one Name. He doesn't mock the readers or the bead-counters. He lists them, and then sets down his own plain sentence. Close by, Guru Nanak speaks to yogis in their own language. In paraphrase: awareness of the Word is my horn, the singi, which the people hear; honor is my bag, and the Name is the alms I receive. A yogi's tools become pictures of the inner life. That's Ramkali's opening calm: not a pile of methods, one Name. Now hold this week up. The ballad, sung with the Name in the mouth. Kabir's joy, mad with praise. Three Bhagats closing Bilaval, one with a blunt question. A sesame seed of effort, never lost. The Guru's image, carried as the Word. And an elephant that bowed. Two ragas behind you, a third begun.
screen: `SANSKRIT, PURANAS, PRAYER BEADS.` · `I KNOW ONLY YOUR ONE NAME.` · `THE YOGI'S HORN, TURNED INWARD.` · `A WEEK, HELD UP.` · then, large: `RAMKALI.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes, rest your hands open, and set down every method for the sit: no counting, no technique. If a word comes, let it be one name you hold dear, then let it go again. If you'd like, read ang 877 first.
Ang 876. Where raga Ramkali begins, and a new stretch of the walk, with Guru Nanak's one Name.
Ramkali: a calm raga, and one Name in place of a pile of methods. A new stretch, begun.

chat.says: SENT THE DEPOSIT. dad hugged me in the yard. now the roommate form says 'describe your faith in one line'
options: Do what Guru Nanak does on ang 876: skip the list of methods and name the one thing you hold.
List everything you practice and read, so they can tell how serious you are about it.

chat.meaning: Ramkali opens with Guru Nanak listing others' methods and saying he knows only the one Name: simple, not a résumé.
